subject.title: RFC: OpenShell session workers and local inference

question: Should OpenClaw standardize provider-authenticated worker transport and worker-local inference as generic core contracts for the plugin-gated OpenShell worker design?
rationale: The proposal intentionally expands core protocol, persisted lease state, provider/model routing, and credential boundaries; whether those abstractions belong in core and their stability level requires maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Advance after hardening
options.body: Keep the RFC draft while adding the missing metadata, maintainer discussion, threat model, compatibility plan, and inspectable live proof, then consider acceptance.

options.title: Narrow to plugin scope
options.body: Accept only OpenShell-owned provisioning initially and defer generic worker-local inference or transport APIs until another provider proves the abstraction.

options.title: Defer the direction
options.body: Leave Gateway-proxy inference as the only supported worker path and pause the RFC until core worker contracts mature further.

recommendation.title: Advance after hardening
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC draft while adding the missing metadata, maintainer discussion, threat model, compatibility plan, and inspectable live proof, then consider acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their documented agents and security ownership best matches the cross-cutting protocol and credential-boundary decision.
